description: Deploy a published Image_Pair of Remote Tic-Tac-Toe by Release_Tag, or restore the tag recorded as previous. The commands are fixed by this document; the caller supplies only the two parameters below.

ReleaseTag.description: The 40-character lowercase commit SHA whose Image_Pair is to be deployed. IGNORED when Mode is fallback, where the tag is read from release.env on the instance instead. It stays required because SSM 2.2 has no conditional parameters; pass the current tag, or any valid SHA.

Mode.description: deploy advances the previous-tag pointer and deploys ReleaseTag. fallback deploys the recorded PREVIOUS_RELEASE_TAG and leaves that pointer untouched. diagnose changes nothing and prints the state Compose reports.

runCommand: #!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
# No doubled curly brace may appear anywhere below except a reference to
# ReleaseTag or Mode -- including inside a comment. SSM uses that delimiter for
# its own parameter substitution, so a Go template in `docker inspect --format`
# would be read as a parameter reference and the document would fail. That is why
# labels are read with jq and containers are resolved with `compose ps -q`.
REQUESTED='{{ ReleaseTag }}'
MODE='{{ Mode }}'
DIR=/srv/tic-tac-toe
ENVFILE="$DIR/deploy/release.env"
APP=ghcr.io/mirkovicuk/tic-tac-toe-app
WEB=ghcr.io/mirkovicuk/tic-tac-toe-web
command -v jq >/dev/null || { echo 'jq is required by this document and is not installed'; exit 69; }
# Read-only, and deliberately before the lock: it exists to observe a deployment
# that has gone wrong, including one still in progress, so taking the lock would
# make it useless in exactly that case. It changes nothing and always exits 0.
# It is here rather than in the workflow because the deployment role is permitted
# to run this document and nothing else -- there is no route to `docker compose ps`
# from the runner, and Req 5.5 asks for the health Compose reports for `app`.
# Order matters, and it is not arbitrary. GetCommandInvocation caps
# StandardOutputContent at 24000 characters and truncates the END, so the cheap
# high-value sections are printed first and the log dump last. Measured on an idle
# instance: 17694 characters total, of which 20 lines of `web` were 13586 -- one
# Caddy access line is a JSON object carrying every request and response header.
# Under real traffic that section alone would exceed the cap and take whatever
# followed it with it, which is why `web` is 5 lines and goes last.
if [[ "$MODE" == diagnose ]]; then
echo '--- release.env'; cat "$ENVFILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 'absent'
echo '--- git'; sudo -u ssm-user git -C "$DIR" log --oneline -1 2>&1 || true
echo '--- compose ps'; docker compose --env-file "$ENVFILE" ps -a 2>&1 || true
echo '--- disk'; df -h / 2>&1 || true
echo '--- app logs'; docker compose --env-file "$ENVFILE" logs --tail=50 --no-color app 2>&1 || true
echo '--- web logs'; docker compose --env-file "$ENVFILE" logs --tail=5 --no-color web 2>&1 || true
exit 0
fi
# One deployment at a time, enforced on the instance. GitHub's concurrency group
# serialises workflow runs, but a person running send-command by hand is outside
# that, and two runs would interleave on one working directory and one env file.
exec 9>"$DIR/deploy/.deploy.lock"
flock -n 9 || { echo 'another deployment is in progress on this instance'; exit 70; }
[[ -f "$ENVFILE" ]] || { echo "missing $ENVFILE; seed it before deploying"; exit 65; }
CURRENT=$(grep -E '^RELEASE_TAG=' "$ENVFILE" | cut -d= -f2 || true)
PREVIOUS=$(grep -E '^PREVIOUS_RELEASE_TAG=' "$ENVFILE" | cut -d= -f2 || true)
# In fallback the instance decides what to deploy, because it is the only thing
# that authoritatively knows the previous tag. The caller does not have to know.
if [[ "$MODE" == fallback ]]; then
TAG="$PREVIOUS"
[[ -n "$TAG" ]] || { echo 'no PREVIOUS_RELEASE_TAG recorded; no fallback is possible'; exit 71; }
KEEP="$PREVIOUS"
else
TAG="$REQUESTED"
# Advance the pointer only when the tag actually changes, so redeploying what
# is already running cannot collapse the fallback target onto the current one.
if [[ "$TAG" != "$CURRENT" ]]; then KEEP="$CURRENT"; else KEEP="$PREVIOUS"; fi
fi
[[ "$TAG" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { echo "resolved tag '$TAG' is not a 40-character hex SHA"; exit 64; }
echo "mode=$MODE current=$CURRENT previous=$PREVIOUS deploying=$TAG keeping_previous=$KEEP"
# Repository operations run as the owning user. Run Command executes as root, and
# git as root in a directory owned by ssm-user fails with a dubious-ownership
# error that reads as a repository fault rather than the permissions one it is.
sudo -u ssm-user git -C "$DIR" fetch --depth 1 origin "$TAG"
sudo -u ssm-user git -C "$DIR" checkout --quiet --detach "$TAG"
# Pull both before recreating either, so a pull that succeeds for one image and
# fails for the other cannot leave a mismatched pair running.
docker pull "$APP:$TAG"
docker pull "$WEB:$TAG"
# Reclaim disk by NAME, not with `image prune`. Untagged-only pruning frees
# nothing here, because every image carries a tag; and `prune -a` would remove
# whatever is not running, which is exactly the previous pair the fallback needs.
KEEPIDS=$(mktemp)
for ref in "$APP:$TAG" "$WEB:$TAG" "$APP:$KEEP" "$WEB:$KEEP"; do
[[ "$ref" == *: ]] && continue
docker image inspect "$ref" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.[0].Id' >> "$KEEPIDS" || true
done
for id in $(docker image ls --quiet --no-trunc "$APP") $(docker image ls --quiet --no-trunc "$WEB"); do
grep -qxF "$id" "$KEEPIDS" || { echo "removing image $id"; docker rmi "$id" || true; }
done
rm -f "$KEEPIDS"
AVAIL=$(df --output=avail -BG / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
(( AVAIL >= 2 )) || { echo "only ${AVAIL}G free after reclaiming; refusing to deploy"; exit 66; }
# The env file is promoted only after Compose succeeds. Written first, a failed
# `up` would leave the file naming a release that never ran -- and the next good
# deployment would then record that never-ran tag as the fallback target.
TMP=$(mktemp "$DIR/deploy/release.env.XXXXXX")
printf 'RELEASE_TAG=%s\nPREVIOUS_RELEASE_TAG=%s\n' "$TAG" "$KEEP" > "$TMP"
# --wait blocks until every service with a healthcheck reports healthy and exits
# non-zero otherwise. Without it `up -d` returns success for a container that
# starts and dies two seconds later.
docker compose --env-file "$TMP" up -d --wait
mv "$TMP" "$ENVFILE"
chown ssm-user: "$ENVFILE"
chmod 600 "$ENVFILE"
# Assert, do not merely report. The label is written by the build, so comparing it
# is independent of what Compose was told -- and Compose may decide not to
# recreate a container at all, in which case a stale one would otherwise pass.
for svc in app web; do
CID=$(docker compose --env-file "$ENVFILE" ps -q "$svc")
[[ -n "$CID" ]] || { echo "service $svc is not running"; exit 68; }
REV=$(docker inspect "$CID" | jq -r '.[0].Config.Labels["org.opencontainers.image.revision"] // "unset"')
echo "$svc revision=$REV"
[[ "$REV" == "$TAG" ]] || { echo "$svc is running $REV, expected $TAG"; exit 67; }
done
docker compose --env-file "$ENVFILE" images
# release.env holds Release_Tags and nothing else. Its contents are echoed into
# SSM command output, which the deployment role can read, so no secret may ever
# be added to it. Secrets belong in deploy/app.env, which is never printed.
cat "$ENVFILE"
echo "deployed $TAG successfully"
